memory_candidates.content: When a concurrently-dispatched sibling task has an unstaged, in-flight edit to a file you also need to touch (e.g. refreshing a 'Last verified' date at the end of a README both tasks are editing), `git add -- <path>` and `git commit -- <path>` BOTH read from the working tree, not the index, so neither can commit only your own hunk while leaving the sibling's hunk unstaged. The safe technique: (1) `git diff -- <path> > sibling.patch` to capture the sibling's unstaged hunk, (2) `git apply -R sibling.patch` to make the working tree match what you want staged, (3) `git add`/commit normally (or `git apply --cached` your own hunk directly if it's not yet in the working tree at all), (4) `git apply sibling.patch` to restore the sibling's hunk in the working tree afterward, verified unchanged via `git diff` before/after.

In this repo's Lean docstrings/READMEs, citing a refutation or probe result from specs/archive/ uses the form: declaration name in backticks, followed by a parenthesised relative path, with NO line number (e.g. `Probe476.fmp_false` (`specs/archive/476_.../evidence/fmp-hypothesis-is-false.lean`)). A line number here would fail C20's file.lean:NNN citation check on a path outside the live tree structure that check expects; the no-line-number, declaration-name-plus-path form is the established convention (mirrored from WitnessFamily/README.md:24-25) and passes the gate.
